The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[def-function]],
> [[def-natural-numbers]]) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** [[def-choice-function]] and
[[def-axiom-of-choice]] select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and [[def-countable-choice]] does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ ([[def-power-set]], [[def-cartesian-product]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]); a natural is the set of its predecessors ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense ([[def-chain]]). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Let $M$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ and the curvature convention of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Take a smooth real
two-form $F$ and smooth current vector $j$ on $U$, with
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ under the adopted convention of
[[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. A chosen smooth matter model supplies a smooth
symmetric covariant tensor $T^m_{ab}$ on $U$ and the current $j$; this postulate
does not assert that arbitrary independently prescribed $T^m$ and $j$ arise
from a matter model.

Define the Einstein tensor by $G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$, using the curvature contractions of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and define the smooth-field electromagnetic
stress tensor by

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

For constant cosmological parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, adopt the additional equation-based gravitational
field law

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}\right).$$

Here $c>0$, $G_N>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ have the SI roles and units fixed in
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]; in length coordinates, $G_{ab}$ and
$\Lambda g_{ab}$ have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ and $T^m$
have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\kappa_E$ has units
$\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. The source-free and sourced Maxwell equations remain
smooth-field postulates: point or sheet sources, distribution-valued products,
material excitation laws, and a global potential are outside this scope.

This is an equation-based adoption. It does not assume or imply the existence
of a matter action and is not derived from an action principle. The sources give
formulations in their own conventions; they motivate comparison but do not
establish a physical law or a solution-existence theorem.

Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, metric-selected
connection, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, two-form field, and SI conventions stated in
[[def-emg-geometry-units]] and [[def-emg-strict-charged-barotropic-system]].
On an open set $U$ of that spacetime, let $\epsilon:U\to J$ be a smooth
rest-energy-density scalar, let $u$ be a smooth future-directed vector field
with $g(u,u)=-1$, and let $Z:U\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth charge-per-particle
scalar. Here $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open interval, $\epsilon$ and
$p(\epsilon)$ have units J m$^{-3}$ = Pa, $u$ is dimensionless, and $Z$ has
units C. In this adopted model, the word *barotropic* means that pressure is a
function of rest-energy density alone.

Adopt a smooth equation of state $p:J\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0,\qquad 0<p'(\epsilon)<1$$
for every $\epsilon\in J$. The dimensionless derivative gives the model's
barotropic characteristic speed $c_{\mathrm s}:=c\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}$, so
this selection requires $0<c_{\mathrm s}<c$. Fix $\epsilon_*\in J$ and a
positive normalization $N_*>0$ with units m$^{-3}$, and define
$$N(\epsilon):=N_*\exp\!\left(\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon} \frac{dz}{z+p(z)}\right).$$
For each $\epsilon\in J$, the closed segment between $\epsilon_*$ and
$\epsilon$ is compact and contained in $J$; the smooth integrand is finite
there. Its integral is dimensionless, so $N(\epsilon)>0$ has units m$^{-3}$.
Within this model, $N$ is the EOS-defined number-density variable and $N_*$
is its chosen normalization. This definition makes no claim that a microscopic
particle theory derives $N$ for every EOS.

Adopt the charged-fluid current and matter stress tensor
$$j^a:=cN(\epsilon)Zu^a,\qquad T_{m,ab}:=(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))u_a u_b+p(\epsilon)g_{ab},$$
and the material balance and advection equations
$$\nabla^aT_{m,ab}=F_{bc}j^c,\qquad u^a\nabla_aZ=0.$$
Thus $j$ is a smooth four-current with components in A m$^{-2}$, and $T_m$
has components in Pa in length coordinates $x^0=ct$. The balance law adopts
the Lorentz-force density with the same field and current conventions as the
chosen Einstein-Maxwell formulation. Charge-per-particle is carried along the
fluid flow. Current conservation is not an additional adopted material law.

This is a physical postulate for smooth classical matter in the strict interior
regime only. It excludes shocks, vacuum interfaces, free boundaries, degenerate
or superluminal sound speed, finite-conductivity and dissipative currents,
point-charge sources, and arbitrary currents chosen independently of the
fluid. The cited treatments motivate the perfect-fluid and charged-current
structures in their own conventions; they do not establish this exact EOS
normalization, the $Z$ transport choice, or the physical applicability of this
model. No matter action, experiment, or universal material law is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice. Use the model, stress tensors, constants, $(-,+,+,+)$ signature, Maxwell signs, and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ convention of [[def-emg-strict-charged-barotropic-system]]. Let $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, let $p=p(\epsilon)$ be smooth on an open interval $J$, and assume $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on a compact interval $K_\epsilon\Subset J$ containing the initial density values.

For smooth Cauchy data on a smooth oriented three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, let $h$ be a Riemannian metric and $K\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*\Sigma)$. Let $\mathfrak n$ be the future unit normal in the initial bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb R\mathfrak n\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_0(a\mathfrak n+X,b\mathfrak n+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Take $\epsilon_0,Z_0\in C^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb R)$, $u_0\in C^\infty(\Sigma,\mathcal V)$, and $e,b\in\Gamma(T\Sigma)$; $e,b$ are the spatial electric and magnetic fields in the $e=E/c$, $b=B$ convention, with units tesla, while $\epsilon_0$ has units J m$^{-3}$, $Z_0$ coulomb, $K$ m$^{-1}$, $u_0$ dimensionless, and $j_0$ A m$^{-2}$, as in [[def-emg-strict-charged-barotropic-system]]. Require $g_0(u_0,u_0)=-1$, $u_0$ future-directed, and $\epsilon_0(\Sigma)\subset K_\epsilon$. Define the unique initial two-form $F_0\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2\mathcal V^*)$ by $e_i=F_0(\mathsf e_i,\mathfrak n)$ and $b_i=\tfrac12\varepsilon_i{}^{jk}F_0(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$ in every oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $(\mathsf e_i)$; existence and uniqueness follow from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Put $T_0=T_{m,0}+T_{\mathrm{EM},0}$ and $j_0=cN(\epsilon_0)Z_0u_0$ using the same definition. Assume the Einstein constraints

$$R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(\mathfrak n,X)$$

for every $X\in T\Sigma$, where $D$ is the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, and the sourced Maxwell constraints

$$\operatorname{div}_h e=-\mu_0g(j_0,\mathfrak n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_h b=0.$$

Then:

**(a) Torus Sobolev branch.** If $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ ([[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]), $s\ge5$ is an integer, $h\in H^{s+1}$, and $K,e,b,\epsilon_0,u_0,Z_0\in H^s$ (with the same strict compact admissibility), there is $T>0$ and a solution of the full Einstein–Maxwell–fluid equations on $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3$ in harmonic gauge. In periodic charts, $g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C^0H^s$, $\partial_tg\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, and $F,\epsilon,u,Z\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$. The fields satisfy the equations classically; uniqueness holds for the corresponding reduced system on common intervals with common compact admissible bounds.

**(b) Smooth geometric branch.** For the smooth data on arbitrary $\Sigma$ above, there is a smooth time-oriented local development on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$, solving the full coupled equations and inducing exactly $(h,K,F_0,\epsilon_0,u_0,Z_0)$. It is unique near the initial surface up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $F,\epsilon,u,Z$. No uniform time width for noncompact $\Sigma$, global existence, shock continuation, vacuum/free-boundary solution, or empirical validity is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $U\subseteq M$ be an open set with smooth observer congruence $n$, let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$, and let $c>0$ be the coordinate conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Define covectors

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $c$ is the positive coordinate-conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with SI unit $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ in its length-coordinate convention. The names electric and magnetic distinguish these two covectors; for arbitrary mathematical $F$ no physical field unit or measurement is assigned.

For each $p\in U$, define the **rest covector space** by

$$\mathcal R^*_{n,p}:=\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n_p)=0\}.$$

The musical isomorphism $\flat_p$ maps the vector rest space $n_p^\perp$ onto $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$: $\alpha\in\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ iff $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,n_p)=\alpha(n_p)=0$. Moreover, $g_p^{-1}(v^\flat,w^\flat)=g_p(v,w)$, so the restriction of $g_p^{-1}$ to $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ is positive definite by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The covectors $E_p$ and $B_p$ annihilate $n_p$; define $\langle E,B\rangle_n(p):=g_p^{-1}(E_p,B_p)$. Then

$$F=n^\flat\wedge E/c+\star_g(n^\flat\wedge B),$$

$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=2\bigl(\langle B,B\rangle_n-\langle E,E\rangle_n/c^2\bigr),\qquad F\wedge F=-\frac{2}{c}\langle E,B\rangle_n\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Equivalently, in any positively oriented future tetrad with $E_0=n$, and with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ in its oriented spatial triad, the components satisfy $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. These are pointwise mathematical decompositions of an arbitrary two-form; no Maxwell equation or physical observation is assumed.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

For the gravitational sector, take Newton's gravitational constant $G_N>0$ with unit $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ and the cosmological constant parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ as primitive parameters of the selected model; no numerical value for either is used here. The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of maps
$u:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^N$ whose pullbacks
$\widetilde u:=u\circ q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ are smooth;
these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when $N=1$).
Equivalently every smooth map $\widetilde u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$
that is $2\pi$-periodic in each coordinate descends to the unique map
$u([x])=\widetilde u(x)$, since periodicity makes this value independent of
$x$ in its equivalence class. For an integer $m\ge0$, define
$C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ similarly by requiring
$\widetilde u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$
([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), and define
$D^\alpha u([x]):=D^\alpha\widetilde u(x)$ for $|\alpha|\le m$.
Derivatives of a periodic $C^m$ map are periodic, so these values are
well-defined, with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|(D^\alpha u)(x)|,$$
where the multi-index derivative is that of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]].

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when the representative $G(t,x,u):=F(t,q(x),u)$ is
locally the restriction of a smooth Euclidean map: for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb R^3\times O$ there are an open neighborhood
$V\subseteq\mathbb R^{4+m}$ and $\widetilde G\in C^\infty(V;\mathbb R^{m'})$
with $\widetilde G=G$ on $V\cap(I\times\mathbb R^3\times O)$.
For open $I$ this is the ordinary Euclidean definition. For nonopen $I$
it is the local extension convention at included endpoints, also admitting
a singleton interval. On a nondegenerate interval endpoint time derivatives
are the limits of interior derivatives; on a singleton no time derivative
is specified without choosing an extension. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be an open set carrying a fixed smooth **background metric**
$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel
symbols in any chart are $\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the same symbol
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ denotes those of $g$. Let $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$
be constants and let $T$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]), the **matter stress-energy
tensor**, with $T=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ its metric trace
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Reduced Einstein equation.** The **reduced Einstein equation** for the
pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

**(d) Einstein residual.** The **Einstein residual** of a pair $(g,T)$ is the
smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$
with $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ the scalar curvature
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein
equation exactly when $E=0$.

**(e) Constraint equations.** If $g$ is defined on a neighborhood of a spacelike
hypersurface $\Sigma$ with future unit normal field $\mathfrak n$ and tangential
frame $(e_i)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]), the
**constraint residuals** are the functions $E(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)$ and
$E(\mathfrak n,e_i)$ on $\Sigma$; that these are the normal and
normal-tangential projections of the field equation, and that they agree with
the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations of the initial data, is
recorded in [[lem-gr-constraint-projections]] and
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

The definition introduces the objects only. The principal part of (b), its
first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction, the identity expressing $E$ through
$H$, the wave equation satisfied by $H$ and the propagation of the constraint
residuals are proved in [[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]],
[[thm-gr-reduced-einstein-local-existence]],
[[lem-gr-einstein-residual-and-subsidiary-identity]] and
[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ be a coordinate neighborhood in an oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, foliated by spacelike $s$-levels. Write
$$g=-\alpha^2ds^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i ds)(dx^j+\beta^j ds),\qquad \alpha>0,\qquad h=(h_{ij})>0,$$
and let $n=\alpha^{-1}(\partial_s-\beta^i\partial_i)$ be the future unit normal. On a smaller neighborhood choose a positively oriented orthonormal spatial frame $(\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ by Gram–Schmidt. Let $D$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$, define $\operatorname{div}_h v:=D_iv^i$ and $(\operatorname{curl}_h v)_i:=\epsilon_i{}^{jk}D_jv_k$, and define the spatial cross product by $(u\times v)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$ in this frame. For a smooth real two-form $F$, define the real spatial components $e_i:=F(\mathsf e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$, with $\epsilon_{123}=1$; thus $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$ in the adapted tetrad. Assume the source-free model of draft definition [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], whose actual equations are $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=0$; its draft status and manifest omission are recorded in [L1].

The six evolution equations for $(e,b)$ have principal part
$$n(e)-\operatorname{curl}_h b=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b),\qquad n(b)+\operatorname{curl}_h e=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b).$$
For a spatial covector $\xi$, let $C(\xi)v:=\xi^\sharp\times v$ in the oriented orthonormal frame. Set $\theta^0:=\alpha ds=-g(n,\cdot)$ and decompose any spacetime covector as $\zeta=\zeta(n)\theta^0+\zeta_\perp$, where $\zeta_\perp(n)=0$ and $|\zeta_\perp|_h$ is its spatial norm. The spatial principal block is the linear map on $\mathbb R^3\oplus\mathbb R^3$ defined by $S(\xi)(u,v)=(-C(\xi)v,C(\xi)u)$. It is real symmetric, has eigenvalues $0,0,|\xi|,|\xi|,-|\xi|,-|\xi|$, and satisfies $\|S(\xi)\|=|\xi|$. Therefore the principal symbol $P(\zeta)=\zeta(n)I_6+S(\zeta_\perp)$ is positive definite for every covector with $\zeta(n)>|\zeta_\perp|_h$. In the adapted coordinates its time matrix is $\alpha^{-1}I_6$, and every coordinate spatial matrix is symmetric. Derivatives of the frame and metric enter only as smooth lower-order coefficients depending on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,e,b)$; in a first-order metric state they are zero-order terms. The remaining two Maxwell equations are the constraints $\operatorname{div}_h e=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_h b=0$.

Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on a smooth oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the connection, Hodge star, and tensor $Q_{ab}=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. For a smooth vector field $J$, suppose

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b.$$

Then $Q_{ab}$ is symmetric and trace-free, and the SI-normalized stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}$ satisfies

$$\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=-F_{bc}J^c.$$

In the source-free case $J=0$, $\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=0$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, put $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$, $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$, and $(e\times b)_i:=\epsilon_{ijk}e_jb_k$. Then

$$T^{\rm EM}(n,n)=\frac{|e|^2+|b|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{\rm EM}(n,\mathfrak e_i)=-\frac{(e\times b)_i}{\mu_0}.$$

These are pointwise tensor identities. In the SI interpretation $e=E/c$ and $b=B$ have units tesla; no measurement or physical applicability claim is included.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[def-function]],
> [[def-natural-numbers]]) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** [[def-choice-function]] and
[[def-axiom-of-choice]] select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and [[def-countable-choice]] does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ ([[def-power-set]], [[def-cartesian-product]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]); a natural is the set of its predecessors ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense ([[def-chain]]). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Use the oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, metric-selected Levi-Civita connection, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, two-form $F$, Einstein tensor $G$, and SI tensor conventions of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. In particular, $F$ is a smooth real section of $\Lambda^2T^*M$, $x^0=ct$ is a length coordinate, the electromagnetic stress is

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\mu_0^{-1}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),$$

and the sourced Maxwell convention is $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=\mu_0\iota_j\operatorname{vol}_g$, equivalently $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. These are mathematical model equations, not claims that the model describes nature.

Choose an open real interval $J$ and a smooth equation of state $p:J\to\mathbb R$ such that $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ for every $\epsilon\in J$. The rest-energy density $\epsilon:M\to J$ and pressure $p(\epsilon)$ have SI units J m$^{-3}$=Pa; $p$ depends only on $\epsilon$, which is the meaning of *barotropic* here. Fix $\epsilon_*\in J$ and a constant $N_*>0$ with units m$^{-3}$ and define the positive EOS scalar

$$N(\epsilon)=N_*\exp\!\left(\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{dz}{z+p(z)}\right).$$

For each $\epsilon\in J$, the closed interval between $\epsilon_*$ and $\epsilon$ is a compact subset of $J$, so the smooth integrand has a finite ordinary integral there. The exponent is dimensionless and $N(\epsilon)>0$. This is an EOS-defined number-density variable and normalization, not a microscopic particle derivation.

Let $u$ be a smooth future-directed vector field with $g(u,u)=-1$, and let $Z:M\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth scalar with units coulomb, interpreted within this model as charge per number-density unit. Define the current and matter stress by

$$j^a=cN(\epsilon)Z u^a,\qquad T_{m,ab}=(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))u_a u_b+p(\epsilon)g_{ab}.$$

Here $u$ is dimensionless, $j$ has SI component units A m$^{-2}$, and $T_m$ has units Pa in the $x^0=ct$ convention. The *strict charged barotropic system* is the smooth tensor system

$$\nabla^aT_{m,ab}=F_{bc}j^c,\qquad u^a\nabla_aZ=0,$$

coupled to the stated sourced Maxwell equations and

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa(T_{m,ab}+T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}),\qquad \kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4>0,\quad \Lambda\in\mathbb R.$$

The first equation is the charged-fluid energy-momentum balance; its Lorentz-force term is orthogonal to $u$ by antisymmetry of $F$. The second transports the charge-per-particle scalar along the fluid flow. No independent current continuity law is added: it is derived in [[lem-emg-charged-fluid-current-conservation]]. No dust, shock, vacuum interface, free boundary, degenerate sound speed, superluminal sound speed, finite-conductivity law, or point-charge source is included.

Assume Countable Choice for the enthalpy integral. Let smooth fields satisfy [[def-emg-strict-charged-barotropic-system]], with $\epsilon\in J$, $u$ future unit timelike, and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Put $c_s=\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}$ and use the enthalpy coordinate

$$r(\epsilon)=\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{\sqrt{p'(z)}}{z+p(z)}\,dz.$$

On a local chart with a smooth frame $e_1,e_2,e_3$ for the positive-definite subbundle $u^\perp$, the energy and momentum equations are equivalent to

$$u^a\nabla_a r+c_s\nabla_a u^a=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_a u_b+c_s(\delta_b{}^a+u_bu^a)\nabla_a r=\frac{F_{bc}j^c}{\epsilon+p},\qquad u^a\nabla_aZ=0.$$

In smooth local coordinates on the unit-velocity hyperboloid, the principal bilinear form on fluid variations $(a,v,z)$ and $(a',v',z')$, with $v,v'\in u^\perp$, is

$$Q_\zeta((a,v,z),(a',v',z'))=\zeta(u)\bigl(aa'+g(v,v')+zz'\bigr)+c_s\bigl(a\zeta(v')+a'\zeta(v)\bigr).$$

It is symmetric and positive definite for every timelike covector $\zeta$ with $\zeta(u)>0$. The Lorentz-force term is algebraic in $(g,F,\epsilon,u,Z)$ and therefore changes only the lower-order term. The transport equation for $Z$ contributes the positive scalar block $\zeta(u)$ and has no principal cross terms.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of maps
$u:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^N$ whose pullbacks
$\widetilde u:=u\circ q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ are smooth;
these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when $N=1$).
Equivalently every smooth map $\widetilde u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$
that is $2\pi$-periodic in each coordinate descends to the unique map
$u([x])=\widetilde u(x)$, since periodicity makes this value independent of
$x$ in its equivalence class. For an integer $m\ge0$, define
$C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ similarly by requiring
$\widetilde u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$
([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), and define
$D^\alpha u([x]):=D^\alpha\widetilde u(x)$ for $|\alpha|\le m$.
Derivatives of a periodic $C^m$ map are periodic, so these values are
well-defined, with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|(D^\alpha u)(x)|,$$
where the multi-index derivative is that of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]].

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when the representative $G(t,x,u):=F(t,q(x),u)$ is
locally the restriction of a smooth Euclidean map: for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb R^3\times O$ there are an open neighborhood
$V\subseteq\mathbb R^{4+m}$ and $\widetilde G\in C^\infty(V;\mathbb R^{m'})$
with $\widetilde G=G$ on $V\cap(I\times\mathbb R^3\times O)$.
For open $I$ this is the ordinary Euclidean definition. For nonopen $I$
it is the local extension convention at included endpoints, also admitting
a singleton interval. On a nondegenerate interval endpoint time derivatives
are the limits of interior derivatives; on a singleton no time derivative
is specified without choosing an extension. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Adopt the equation-based Einstein-Maxwell field postulate
[[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] and the smooth material closure of
[[post-emg-strict-charged-fluid-model]], with the SI, signature, and coordinate
conventions of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Thus the spacetime field equations
are $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, and
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa(T_{m,ab}+T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}),\qquad \kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4,$$
while the fluid contributes exactly its adopted $T_m,j$ and material balance
equations. No matter action is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice.
Let $p=p(\epsilon)$ be smooth on an open interval $J$, and let
$K_\epsilon\Subset J$ be a compact interval containing the initial density
values, on which $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Take
$\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, and let
$\mathfrak n$ be its future unit normal. Let $h$ be a Riemannian metric and
let $K\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*\Sigma)$ use the second fundamental
form convention
$$K(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\mathfrak n,Y).$$
The initial normal bundle is
$\mathcal V:=\mathbb R\mathfrak n\oplus T\Sigma$ with
$$g_0(a\mathfrak n+X,b\mathfrak n+Y):=-ab+h(X,Y).$$
Let $\epsilon_0,Z_0$ be smooth scalar fields, $u_0$ a smooth future unit
timelike section of $\mathcal V$ satisfying $g_0(u_0,u_0)=-1$, and $e,b$
smooth spatial vector fields
representing $E/c$ and $B$ in an oriented orthonormal frame. Their units are
J m$^{-3}$, C, dimensionless, and tesla, respectively; $K$ has units m$^{-1}$.
The components of the smooth initial two-form $F_0$ are defined in every
positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $(\mathsf e_i)$ by
$$e_i=F_0(\mathsf e_i,\mathfrak n),\qquad b_i=\tfrac12\varepsilon_i{}^{jk}F_0(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k), \qquad \varepsilon_{123}=1.$$
This fixes all six independent components of $F_0$. Set
$j_0=cN(\epsilon_0)Z_0u_0$ and $T_0=T_{m,0}+T_{\mathrm{EM},0}$ from the
adopted model.

Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$,
$\tau:=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$,
$|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$,
$(\operatorname{div}_hK)_j:=h^{ik}(D_iK)_{kj}$, and $R(h)$ for the scalar
curvature of $h$. Assume the complete Einstein and sourced Maxwell initial
constraints
$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T_0(\mathfrak n,X)$$
for every tangent vector $X$, and
$$\operatorname{div}_h e=-\mu_0g_0(j_0,\mathfrak n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_h b=0.$$

Then the adopted equation-based fluid model has the following conditional
local developments.

**(a) Torus Sobolev branch.** If
$\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ with the periodic
Sobolev spaces of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], assigning each
spatial period length $2\pi\,\mathrm m$ in the length-coordinate convention of
[F6]. Assume $s\ge5$ is an integer, $h\in H^{s+1}$ and
$K,e,b,\epsilon_0,u_0,Z_0\in H^s$, with the same strict compact
admissibility. Then there is $T>0$ and a solution on
$(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3$ in the harmonic gauge of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], relative to the fixed
background used by [[thm-emg-local-charged-barotropic-development]]. In
periodic charts,
$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C^0H^s$,
$\partial_tg\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, and
$F,\epsilon,u,Z\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$. The equations hold
classically, and the reduced solution is unique on common intervals with common
compact admissible bounds.

**(b) Smooth geometric branch.** For smooth data on any $\Sigma$ above, there
is a smooth time-oriented solution on an open variable-width neighborhood of
$\{0\}\times\Sigma$, inducing exactly $(h,K,F_0,\epsilon_0,u_0,Z_0)$. It is
unique near the initial surface up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry matching $F,\epsilon,u,Z$. No uniform time width for noncompact
$\Sigma$, global existence, shock continuation, vacuum/free-boundary solution,
or empirical validity is asserted.

This is a model deduction. It does not assert that the postulates describe
nature.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, metric-selected
connection, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, two-form field, and SI conventions stated in
[[def-emg-geometry-units]] and [[def-emg-strict-charged-barotropic-system]].
On an open set $U$ of that spacetime, let $\epsilon:U\to J$ be a smooth
rest-energy-density scalar, let $u$ be a smooth future-directed vector field
with $g(u,u)=-1$, and let $Z:U\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth charge-per-particle
scalar. Here $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open interval, $\epsilon$ and
$p(\epsilon)$ have units J m$^{-3}$ = Pa, $u$ is dimensionless, and $Z$ has
units C. In this adopted model, the word *barotropic* means that pressure is a
function of rest-energy density alone.

Adopt a smooth equation of state $p:J\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0,\qquad 0<p'(\epsilon)<1$$
for every $\epsilon\in J$. The dimensionless derivative gives the model's
barotropic characteristic speed $c_{\mathrm s}:=c\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}$, so
this selection requires $0<c_{\mathrm s}<c$. Fix $\epsilon_*\in J$ and a
positive normalization $N_*>0$ with units m$^{-3}$, and define
$$N(\epsilon):=N_*\exp\!\left(\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon} \frac{dz}{z+p(z)}\right).$$
For each $\epsilon\in J$, the closed segment between $\epsilon_*$ and
$\epsilon$ is compact and contained in $J$; the smooth integrand is finite
there. Its integral is dimensionless, so $N(\epsilon)>0$ has units m$^{-3}$.
Within this model, $N$ is the EOS-defined number-density variable and $N_*$
is its chosen normalization. This definition makes no claim that a microscopic
particle theory derives $N$ for every EOS.

Adopt the charged-fluid current and matter stress tensor
$$j^a:=cN(\epsilon)Zu^a,\qquad T_{m,ab}:=(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))u_a u_b+p(\epsilon)g_{ab},$$
and the material balance and advection equations
$$\nabla^aT_{m,ab}=F_{bc}j^c,\qquad u^a\nabla_aZ=0.$$
Thus $j$ is a smooth four-current with components in A m$^{-2}$, and $T_m$
has components in Pa in length coordinates $x^0=ct$. The balance law adopts
the Lorentz-force density with the same field and current conventions as the
chosen Einstein-Maxwell formulation. Charge-per-particle is carried along the
fluid flow. Current conservation is not an additional adopted material law.

This is a physical postulate for smooth classical matter in the strict interior
regime only. It excludes shocks, vacuum interfaces, free boundaries, degenerate
or superluminal sound speed, finite-conductivity and dissipative currents,
point-charge sources, and arbitrary currents chosen independently of the
fluid. The cited treatments motivate the perfect-fluid and charged-current
structures in their own conventions; they do not establish this exact EOS
normalization, the $Z$ transport choice, or the physical applicability of this
model. No matter action, experiment, or universal material law is asserted.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

$$g=-\alpha^2ds^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i ds)(dx^j+\beta^j ds),\qquad \alpha>0,\qquad h=(h_{ij})>0,$$
and let $n=\alpha^{-1}(\partial_s-\beta^i\partial_i)$ be the future unit normal. On a smaller neighborhood choose a positively oriented orthonormal spatial frame $(\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ by Gram–Schmidt. Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on a smooth oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the connection, Hodge star, and tensor $Q_{ab}=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. For a smooth vector field $J$, suppose

On $J=(0,\infty)$, $p'=w\in(0,1)$ and
$\epsilon+p=(1+w)\epsilon>0$. By [F1] and [F3],
$$N(\epsilon)=N_*\exp\!\left(\frac1{1+w} \int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{dz}{z}\right) =N_*\exp\!\left(\frac{\log(\epsilon/\epsilon_*)}{1+w}\right) =N_*\left(\frac{\epsilon}{\epsilon_*}\right)^{1/(1+w)}.$$
The ratio in the logarithm is dimensionless.

Since $\sqrt{p'(z)}=\sqrt w$, [F2] and [F3] give
$$r(\epsilon)=\frac{\sqrt w}{1+w}\log\!\left(\frac{\epsilon}{\epsilon_*}\right), \qquad r'(\epsilon)=\frac{\sqrt w}{(1+w)\epsilon}>0,$$
so this is the strictly increasing enthalpy coordinate of [F2]. By [F7], the
adopted physical characteristic speed is $c_{\mathrm s}=c\sqrt w\in(0,c)$.

The definition [F4] identifies the torus as the quotient by translations
in $(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$. For any point of $\mathbb R^3$, an open ball of radius
less than $\pi$ is disjoint from each of its nontrivial lattice translates;
the quotient map therefore gives local smooth charts with transition maps that
are translations, so the quotient is a smooth three-manifold without boundary.
The translations preserve both the Euclidean orientation and metric, so these
descend to an orientation and the flat metric $h=\delta$. The continuous
quotient map sends the compact cube $[0,2\pi]^3$ onto the torus, hence the torus
is compact. In these local quotient charts $h$ has constant Euclidean
coefficients, so its Levi-Civita derivative vanishes and its curvature is zero.

For the data in the Example, $j_0=0$ because $Z_0=0$. Also
$T_{m,0}(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)
=(\epsilon_*+p(\epsilon_*))(-1)^2
+p(\epsilon_*)g_0(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=\epsilon_*$,
and $T_{m,0}(\mathfrak n,X)=0$ for every tangent $X$. The electromagnetic
stress vanishes because $e=b=0$.

By step 1.3 the flat torus has $R(h)=0$ and $D h=0$. In three dimensions,
$\tau=\operatorname{tr}_h(Hh)=3H$ and $|K|_h^2=3H^2$, so the Hamiltonian
left side is $9H^2-3H^2=6H^2$. Its right side is
$2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n)=2\kappa\epsilon_*=6H^2$
by the choice of $\epsilon_*$. The density units are
$[3H^2/\kappa]=\mathrm{m}^{-2}/(\mathrm{m\,J}^{-1})=\mathrm{J\,m}^{-3}$
by the stated units and [F8]. Both sides of the momentum constraint vanish
because $H$ is constant and $T_0(\mathfrak n,X)=0$.

The two Maxwell constraints reduce to $\operatorname{div}_h0=0$ and
$-\mu_0g_0(j_0,\mathfrak n)=0$, so both hold. The fields are smooth, and
their density range $\{\epsilon_*\}$ is contained in the compact interval
$K_\epsilon=[\epsilon_*/2,3\epsilon_*/2]\Subset J$. All strict EOS
inequalities hold on $K_\epsilon$ by step 1.1. Thus the complete
smooth-data hypotheses of [F5] hold.
